QASHANI:111:1-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:111:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:111:1-4/r2.claim: His original wealth signifies innate preparatory knowledge and his earnings false belief; neither benefits him because his beliefs do not match reality, and both contribute to torment.
QASHANI:111:1-4/r2.anchor: ما نفعه ماله الأصلي من العلم الاستعدادي الفطري ولا مكسوبه لعدم مطابقة اعتقاده لما في نفس الأمر

QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r3.claim: His wealth and vile earnings did not benefit him at all.
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r3.anchor: ما أغنى عنه ماله ولا كسبه الخبيث - شيئا

QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r4.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r4.claim: An alternative interpretation of “what he earned” is his child.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r5.claim: Aisha says a man's best food is from his own earnings and that his child is also his earning, then reads the verse as referring to Abu Lahab's child.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت اطيب ما اكل الرجل من كسبه ، وان ابنه من كسبه ثم قرات : ما اغنى عنه ماله وما كسب

IBNASHUR:111:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r1.claim: The verse begins a new statement shifting from insult and rebuke to announcing Abū Lahab’s hopeless ruin: his property and earnings will save him from nothing in the afterlife.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r1.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي للانتقال من إنشاء الشتم والتوبيخ

IBNASHUR:111:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r2.claim: The past “did not avail” makes his failure to be saved certain.

IBNASHUR:111:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r3.claim: Mā is negative, though it may also be read as an interrogative expressing rebuke and denial.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية للتوبيخ والإنكار

IBNASHUR:111:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r4.claim: Māl means owned wealth, commonly camels among Arabs; ʿUmar’s saying and a line by Zuhayr attest that usage, while Medinans, Khaybar residents, and Bahrainis often use it for date palms.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r4.anchor: وغلب عند العرب إطلاقه على الإبل

IBNASHUR:111:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r5.claim: The phrase “what he earned” is a relative clause with an optionally omitted object pronoun, meaning what he amassed.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r5.anchor: موصول وصلته والعائد محذوف جوازا لأنه ضمير نصب

IBNASHUR:111:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r6.claim: “What he earned” can mean assets besides livestock—currency, weapons, estates, goods, and food.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r6.anchor: من نقود وسلاح وربع وعروض وطعام

IBNASHUR:111:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:2/r7.claim: Alternatively, “his wealth” includes everything, and “what he earned” specifies his own acquired wealth after inherited property: what he inherited from ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib versus what he himself acquired.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r7.anchor: وهو ما ورثه عن أبيه عبد المطلب وما كسبه هو بنفسه

IBNASHUR:111:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR:111:2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports Abū Lahab claimed he would ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew’s message proved true; the verse was revealed in response.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أن أبا لهب قال

IBNASHUR:111:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:111:2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “what he earned” as his children, since a child is his father’s earning.
IBNASHUR:111:2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { ما كسب } هو ولده

TUSTARI:111:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:111:2/r1.claim: His wealth will not benefit him in the afterlife because he goes to the Fire; what he gained refers to his sons Utba, Utayba, and Muattib.
TUSTARI:111:2/r1.anchor: في الآخرة، إذ صار إلى النار { وما كسب } [2] يعني ولده عتبة وعتيبة ومعتب.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r1.claim: ما كسب is a relative clause with an omitted object pronoun, meaning what Abu Lahab earned or amassed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r1.anchor: { وما كسب } موصول وصلته والعائد محذوف جوازا لأنه ضمير نصب ، والتقدير : وما كسبه ، أي ما جمعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r2.claim: One reading takes his wealth as movable assets such as money, weapons, estates, goods, and food, while what he earned is his personal acquisitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r2.anchor: والمراد به : ما يملكه من غير النعم من نقود وسلاح وربع وعروض وطعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r3.claim: Alternatively, his wealth includes everything; ما كسب then singles out what he personally gained in contrast to inherited property.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بماله : جميع ماله ، ويكون عطف { وما كسب } من ذكر الخاص بعد العام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r4.claim: He reports Abu Lahab saying he would ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew's claim proved true; the verse answered that boast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أن أبا لهب قال : ( إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدي نفسي يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r5.claim: He identifies what Abu Lahab earned as his children, since a child is counted among a father's earnings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { ما كسب } هو ولده فإن الولد من كسب أبيه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r6.claim: The statement means nothing can spare him from Hell; revealed during Abu Lahab's lifetime, it foretold that he would die an unbeliever and thus testified to prophecy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p604/r6.anchor: ونزل هذا القرآن في حياة أبي لهب . وقد مات بعد ذلك كافرا ، فكانت هذه الآية إعلاما بأنه لا يسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r6.claim: Ma aghna can be read as negation—none of his worldly circumstances helped after his punishment was decreed—or as a rhetorical question asking what benefit his wealth and earnings gave him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r6.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون ما نافية، ويكون الكلام خبرا عن أن جميع أحواله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r7.claim: Ma kasab can mean worldly assets, or emphasize that he worked to acquire them rather than receiving them as inheritance or gifts; many exegetes instead take it to mean his sons.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r7.anchor: وما كسب: يراد به عرض الدنيا من عقار ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r8.claim: A hadith says the best thing a man earns is the work of his hand, and his child is among his earnings; Ibn ‘Abbas once called Abu Lahab’s children evil earnings when they fought and one pushed him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r8.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خير ما كسب الرجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r9.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r9.claim: Al-A‘mash and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b read iktasaba, ‘what he acquired,’ instead of kasaba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبي بن كعب: «وما اكتسب»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that when the Prophet called his close kin to God, Abu Lahab said he would ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew spoke truth; the verse answers that boast.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود لما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقربيه إلى الله عز وجل قال أبو لهب إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses mā as nominative, with the sense that Abu Lahab's wealth and earnings did not benefit him; kasaba means his children, as commentators explain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج و ما في موضع رفع المعنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r3.claim: The commentators understand what Abu Lahab earned as his children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r3.anchor: وكذلك قال المفسرون المراد بكسبه هاهنا ولده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r4.claim: Aghnā here has the force of the future: it will avail or benefit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p260/r4.anchor: المراد بكسبه هاهنا ولده و أغنى بمعنى يغني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r2.claim: They interpret Abu Lahab's “gain” as his children.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Abu Lahab hoped to ransom himself from Judgment Day punishment with his wealth and children, prompting the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r3.anchor: فإني أفتدي نفسي يوم القيامة من العذاب بمالي وولدي

KASHSHAF:111:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:2/r1.claim: ‘Mā aghnā’ is either an interrogative with a force of denial in the accusative, or a negation; ‘mā kasaba’ is nominative.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r1.anchor: { مَا أغنى } استفهام في معنى الإنكار ،   ومحله النصب أو نفي { وَمَا كَسَبَ } مرفوع .

KASHSHAF:111:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:2/r2.claim: ‘Mā kasaba’ may be a relative or a verbal noun, meaning what he acquired or his earning.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r2.anchor: وما موصولة أو مصدرية بمعنى : ومكسوبه .   أو : وكسبه .

KASHSHAF:111:2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:2/r3.claim: The phrase may mean his money and profits, his livestock and their offspring and benefits, his inherited wealth and personal earnings, or his old and newly acquired wealth.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r3.anchor: والمعنى : لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله ،   يعني : رأس المال والأرباح .

KASHSHAF:111:2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:111:2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets ‘what he earned’ as his children.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ما كسب ولده .

KASHSHAF:111:2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:2/r5.claim: A family dispute anecdote says Abū Lahab called his children ‘filthy earnings’ after one shoved him while he broke up their fight; a Prophetic report says a man’s child counts among his earnings.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r5.anchor: وحكي أن بني أبي لهب احتكموا إليه ،   فاقتتلوا ،   فقام يحجز بينهم ،

KASHSHAF:111:2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:111:2/r6.claim: The Prophet said that a man’s best food is what he earns and that his child is among his earnings.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r6.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام :  "  إن أطيب ما يأكل الرجل من كسبه ،

KASHSHAF:111:2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF:111:2/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the phrase to mean wealth and wicked work, specifically Abū Lahab’s plot against the Prophet.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r7.anchor: وعن الضحاك : ما ينفعه ماله وعمله الخبيث ،   يعني كيده في عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:111:2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r8.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF:111:2/r8.claim: Qatādah interprets it as work he thought would benefit him, linking it to the verse about deeds made like scattered dust.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r8.anchor: وعن قتادة : عمله الذي ظنّ أنه منه على شيء ،   كقوله : { وَقَدِمْنَا إلى مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنْ عَمَلٍ } [ الفرقان : 23 ]

KASHSHAF:111:2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:2/r9.claim: Abū Lahab reportedly boasted that if his nephew were right, he could ransom himself from the punishment with his wealth and children.
KASHSHAF:111:2/r9.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقاً فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي .

MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r2.claim: His wealth and gains did not avail him; he will enter the flame, and his wife will enter it too.
MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r2.anchor: «ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب سيصلى» (2- 3) سيصلى «نارا ذات لهب وامرأته» (3- 4) أيضا ستصلى..

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r16.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak says the clause asks what protected Abu Lahab from harm.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak also glosses the verb as benefiting him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r18.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r18.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies Abu Lahab’s wealth as his herds of livestock.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r18.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد أغنامه , لأنه كان صاحب سائمة , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r19.claim: Another view takes his wealth to be inherited and acquired assets, respectively called talid and tarif.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r19.anchor: الثاني : أنه أراد تليده وطارفه , والتليد : الموروث , والطارف : المكتسب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r20.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r20.claim: Al-Dahhak reads what Abu Lahab earned as his evil deeds.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas reads what he earned as his children; the Prophet is reported to have said children are among one’s earnings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r21.anchor: الثاني : ولده , قاله ابن عباس . وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( أولادكم من كسبكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r22.claim: Abu Lahab’s son Utba shared his father’s hostility, rejected the revelation of 53:1 and 53:8, and spat toward the Prophet; after the Prophet prayed against him, a lion ate him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r22.anchor: وكان ولده عتبة بن أبي لهب مبالغا في عداوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كأبيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r23.claim: The wealth and earnings failed either to assist Abu Lahab’s hostility toward the Prophet or to shield him from Hell on Judgment Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r23.anchor: أحدهما : في عداوته النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . الثاني : في دفع النار عنه يوم القيامة

MUJAHID:v2p793/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p793/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p793/r1.claim: Mujahid says Abu Lahab’s wealth and earnings refer to his child.
MUJAHID:v2p793/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ماله وما كسب ﴾ يعني ولده

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r9.claim: His wealth cannot help him in the afterlife; what he earned means his sons Utba, Utayba, and Mutabb, since children are a man's earnings.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r9.anchor: في الآخرة { وما كسب } [آية: 2] يعني أولاده عتبة وعتيبة ومتعب لأن ولده من كسبه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r1.claim: Mā is a negator; mā kasab may be a relative noun or a verbal noun, referring to inherited and acquired wealth, old and new assets, or earnings.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r1.anchor: مرفوع وما موصولة أو مصدرية أي ومكسوبة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets what he acquired as his children.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ماكسب ولده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r3.claim: Abū Lahab reportedly said that if his nephew's message were true, he would ransom himself with his wealth and children.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p362/r3.anchor: وروى أنه كان يقول أن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدى منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

NAHHAS:v5p305/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p305/r6.claim: Mā may be accusative as the object of aghnā or have no syntactic case as a negation.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r6.anchor: في ما قولان أحدهما أنها في موضع نصب بأغنى والقول الآخر أنها لا موضع لها من الإعراب

NAHHAS:v5p305/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p305/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mā kasaba means his son; another explanation is all that he acquired.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r7.anchor: ( وما كسب ) فيه قولان أحدهما أنه يراد به ولده هذا قول ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r1.claim: Neither Abu Lahab's accumulated wealth nor the standing he earned could protect him from God's punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r1.anchor: أي ما دفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال، ولا ما كسب من جاه.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r2.claim: Mujahid explains 'what he earned' as his children, since a man's child is among his earnings.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من الولد وولد الرجل من كسبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r3.speaker: الأعمش عن ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r3.claim: Al-A'mash reads 'wa-ma iktasab' and transmits this reading from Ibn Masud.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «وما اكتسب» ورواه عن ابن مسعود.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r4.speaker: أبو الطفيل
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r4.claim: Abu al-Tufayl says Ibn Abbas called Abu Lahab's sons 'the vile earning' after they fought and shoved him while he tried to separate them.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الطفيل: جاء بنو أبي لهب يختصمون عند ابن عباس، فاقتتلوا،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r5.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying the best food a man eats is from his own earnings and that his child is among his earnings.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r5.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Lahab offered to ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew's warning proved true; the verse answered him.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما أنذر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشيرته بالنار،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r7.claim: The first ma may be a negation or a rhetorical question asking what his property gained him.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r7.anchor: و«ما» في قوله: { مآ أغنى }: يجوز أن تكون نفيا، ويجوز أن تكون استفهاما

QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r8.claim: The second ma may mean 'that which he acquired' or function with the verb as a verbal noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:2/r8.anchor: و«ما» الثانية: يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي، ويجوز أن تكون مع الفعل مصدرا

QUTB-ZILAL:111:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:2/r1.claim: Abu Lahab’s wealth and earnings could not benefit him, fend off ruin, or prevent his destruction.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:2/r1.anchor: فلم يغن عنه ماله وسعيه ولم يدفع عنه الهلاك والدمار

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.claim: The creation purpose is worship; al-Kafirun contrasts the Prophet’s obedience and rejection of partners with the unbelievers’ worship of idols, while al-Nasr promises worldly victory and afterlife reward and al-Masad threatens worldly loss and afterlife punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.anchor: ثم بين في سورة : { قل ياأهل * أيها * الكافرون }

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r1.claim: Ma aghna can be a rhetorical question asking what effect Abu Lahab’s wealth and gains could have had against disaster; even Qarun and Solomon could not avert death.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما بمعنى الإنكار

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r2.claim: Alternatively, the wording is a direct statement that wealth and earnings did not help him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r2.anchor: وعلى التقدير الثاني يكون ذلك إخبارا بأن المال

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r3.claim: The phrase ma kasaba is a raised relative or verbal noun, meaning either what he acquired or his earning.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r3.anchor: ما كسب مرفوع وما موصولة أو مصدرية يعني مكسوبه أو كسبه

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r4.claim: Abu Lahab reportedly said that if his nephew’s message were true, he would ransom himself with his wealth and children; this verse answered him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r4.anchor: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وأولادي

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r5.claim: One interpretation distinguishes his capital from profits earned on it.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r5.anchor: لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله يعني رأس المال والأرباح

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes his wealth as livestock and what he gained as their offspring and yield.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r6.anchor: المال هو الماشية وما كسب من نسلها

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r7.claim: A third view distinguishes inherited property from what Abu Lahab earned himself.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r7.anchor: الذي ورثه من أبيه والذي كسبه بنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies what he gained with his children, supported by a hadith calling a man’s child part of his earnings; another report says Abu Lahab called his sons his wicked gains after they knocked him down.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { ما كسبت } ولده

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r9.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the phrase as Abu Lahab’s wealth and evil work, especially his plots against the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r9.anchor: قال الضحاك : ما ينفعه ماله وعمله الخبيث

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r10.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r10.claim: Qatada reads it as deeds Abu Lahab thought would benefit him, like works rendered worthless in the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r10.anchor: قال قتادة : { وما كسب } أي عمله

RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156/r11.claim: Using the past tense is more emphatic than the future wording in al-Layl, as in other Qur’anic statements that use past verbs for certainty.

RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r1.claim: One answer is that wealth and earnings failed to let Abu Lahab defeat the Messenger in his hostility.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r1.anchor: في عداوة الرسول : فلم يغلب عليه

RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r2.claim: Another answer is that wealth and earnings could not save him from the Fire, as the next verse explains.
RAZI-FULL:v32p156#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل لم يغنيا عنه في دفع النار

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.claim: Al-Masad is considered one of the earliest Makkan surahs; its name comes from the final word, said to denote a Hell punishment, and it is also called al-Lahab, “The Flame.”
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.anchor: l-Masad is believed to be among the earliest Makkan

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.claim: Abū Lahab's nickname means “Father of Flame” and refers to his bright red complexion.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.anchor: known by the nickname Abū Lahab, “The Father of Flame,” because of his bright red complexion

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.claim: After the Prophet warned Quraysh from a hill, Abū Lahab cursed him for summoning them; God then revealed the five verses.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.anchor: Then God revealed the five verses

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.speaker: many
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.claim: Many say the surah followed immediately after 26:214; its five short verses describe the Hell punishment of Abū Lahab and his wife.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.anchor: Many say this revelation occurred immediately after the revelation of 26:214

STUDYQURAN:111:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r1.speaker: many
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r1.claim: Many interpret what Abū Lahab earned or committed as referring to his children.
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r1.anchor: What he has earned, or “what he has committed,” is interpreted by many to mean his children

STUDYQURAN:111:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r2.claim: The verse answers Abū Lahab's boast that, if his nephew were right, he would ransom himself with wealth and children.
STUDYQURAN:111:2/r2.anchor: This verse is said to be a response to

TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Abu Lahab's hands and deeds failed; the opening expression is a divine curse, while “and he perished” is a report, supported by ʿAbd Allāh's reading with “already.”
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {تبت يدا أبي لهب} [المسد: 1] دعاء عليه من الله

TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses Abu Lahab's fate as loss and ruin.
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {تبت يدا أبي لهب} [المسد: 1] أي «خسرت وتب

TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd links the verse to Abu Lahab asking whether conversion would give him equal treatment; he curses such a religion, and the verse says his deeds brought ruin.
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله: {تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب} [المسد: 1] قال: التب

TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after the Prophet warned Quraysh from Ṣafā, Abu Lahab cursed him for summoning them, and the sura was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم الصفا، فقال: «يا صباحاه

TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r5.claim: The sura's occasion is also placed after the command to warn the nearest relatives, when Abu Lahab cursed the Prophet for calling them together.
TAB-FULL:v24p714#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه السورة نزلت في أبي لهب، لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما خص بالدعوة عشيرته

TAB-FULL:v24p716/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's report recounts the Prophet summoning Quraysh on Ṣafā, asking if they would believe a warning of cavalry, and Abu Lahab cursing him; the sura followed.
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نزلت {وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين} [الشعراء: 214] قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصفا

TAB-FULL:v24p716/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r2.claim: A second version adds the command to warn the nearest relatives and the Prophet's call to Banū Hāshim and Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib before Abu Lahab's insult.
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين} [الشعراء: 214] ورهطك منهم المخلصين

TAB-FULL:v24p716/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r3.claim: Sufyān says the Prophet called his uncle ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā among those warned; Abu Lahab replied that this was a poor reason to summon them, prompting the verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p716/r3.anchor: عن سفيان، في قوله: تبت يدا أبي لهب قال: حين أرسل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إليه وإلى غيره

TAB-FULL:v24p718/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās called Abu Lahab's fighting sons his “evil earnings” when he intervened between them.
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r1.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل، قال: جاء بنو أبي لهب إلى ابن عباس، فقاموا يختصمون في البيت

TAB-FULL:v24p718/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r2.claim: Mujāhid explicitly identifies “what he acquired” as Abu Lahab's children.
TAB-FULL:v24p718/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {وما كسب} [المسد: 2] قال: ولده هم من كسبه

SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r1.claim: Mā in mā aghnā can be negation or an interrogative object; the interrogative is fronted because it has clause-initial position.
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r1.anchor: يجوز في " ما " النفي والاستفهام، وعلى الثاني تكون منصوبة المحل بما بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r2.claim: Mā kasaba can be a relative pronoun with its referent omitted, a verbal noun meaning his earning, or an interrogative meaning he gained nothing.
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r2.anchor: يجوز في " ما " هذه أن تكون بمعنى الذي، فالعائد محذوف، وأن تكون مصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r3.claim: He takes the interrogative reading of mā kasaba as rhetorically equivalent to a negation: what did he earn? Nothing.
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r3.anchor: يعني: وأي شيء كسب؟ أي: لم يكسب شيئا، قاله الشيخ

SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r4.claim: Treating mā as directly negative is possible on that sense, but the author finds it unpersuasive.
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r4.anchor: فعلى هذا يجوز أن تكون نافية، ويكون المعنى على ما ذكر، وهو غير ظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:111:2/r5.claim: His reading replaces kasaba with اكتسب.

ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r3.speaker: المفسرون
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r3.claim: Commentators say mā kasaba refers to his children; grammatically mā is nominative and the sense is his wealth and what he earned.
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r3.anchor: المفسرون قالوا: ما كسب هاهنا ولده.

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r8.claim: The first ma is negative; the second is relative, meaning his deeds or their effects, or a verbal noun meaning what he earned. Neither wealth nor work saved him from ruin.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r8.anchor: ما الأولى نافية وما الثانية موصولة

TABRISI:111:3-4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:111:3-4/r11.claim: His wealth and acquisitions did not benefit him or ward off God's punishment; “what he acquired” can be a relative clause with its pronoun omitted.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r11.anchor: أي ما نفعه ولا دفع عنه عذاب الله ماله { وما كسبه }

TABRISI:111:3-4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes “what he acquired” to mean his child, since a man's child is counted as his earning; Abu Lahab had threatened to ransom himself with wealth and children.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r12.anchor: يعني ولده لأن ولد الرجل من كسبه وذلك أنه قال لما أنذره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v10p325/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v10p325/r2.claim: After the Prophet warned his relatives, Abu Lahab said he would ransom himself, his property, and his children if his nephew's message were true; the verse says his wealth would not avail him.
THALABI:v10p325/r2.anchor: قال: ابن مسعود: لما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرباءه الى الله سبحانه قال أبو لهب

THALABI:v10p325/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p325/r3.claim: Mā aghnā means what benefits; alternatively, what benefit could his property give him against God's punishment?
THALABI:v10p325/r3.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه ما أغنى أي ما يغني، وقيل: أي شيء أغنى عنه ماله من عذاب الله.

THALABI:v10p325/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v10p325/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the wealth was his flocks and livestock, while what he earned meant his children.
THALABI:v10p325/r4.anchor: قال: أبو العالية: يعني أغنامه، وكان صاحب سائمة ومواش، وما كسب: يعني ولده.

THALABI:v10p325/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r5.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v10p325/r5.claim: Al-A'mash reads wa-ma iktasaba, a reading he transmits from Ibn Masud.
THALABI:v10p325/r5.anchor: قرأ الأعمش (وما أكتسب) ، ورواه عن ابن مسعود.

THALABI:v10p325/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p325/r6.claim: When Abu Lahab's sons fought, Ibn Abbas called them foul earnings, explaining that children are a person's earnings.
THALABI:v10p325/r6.anchor: فغضب ابن عباس فقال: أخرجوا عني الكسب الخبيث، يعني ولده أنهم كسبة

THALABI:v10p325/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p325/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p325/r7.claim: A report from Aisha says the best food a person eats is what he earns, and his child is part of his earnings.
THALABI:v10p325/r7.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إن أطيب ما أكل أحدكم من كسبه وأن ولده من كسبه»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r1.claim: The commentators say neither Abū Lahab’s wealth nor what he acquired could shield him from God’s punishment; “what he acquired” means his child, since a child is a person’s earnings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r1.anchor: - {ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب} (¬10) أي: ما دفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من ماله، وما ولد. (وهو قول كافة أهل التفسير) (¬11).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة وابن سيرين ومجاهد ومقاتل وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾisha, Ibn Sīrīn, Mujāhid, Muqatil, and Qatāda identify his child as his earnings; a Prophetic report that a child is part of one’s earnings supports this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p411#3/r2.anchor: قالوا: وما كسب يعني: ولده؛ لأن ولده من كسبه. قاله ابن # عباس (¬1)، وعائشة (¬2) وابن سيرين (¬3)، (ومجاهد (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5)، وقتادة (¬6)) (¬7):

WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r1.speaker: أبو لهب
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r1.claim: Abu Lahab said that if his nephew were right, he would ransom himself from punishment with his money and children.
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r1.anchor: إنه إن كان ما يقوله ابن أخي حقا ،   فإني أفتدي منه بمالي وولدي

WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r2.claim: His wealth did not benefit him, and what he earned means his children.
WAHIDI-QT:111:2/r2.anchor: { ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب } يعني ولده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r3.speaker: أبو لهب
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r3.claim: Abu Lahab claimed that if his nephew's warning were true, he would ransom himself from the punishment with his wealth and children.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r3.anchor: ولما خوفه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعذاب قال: إنه إن كان ما يقوله ابن أخي حقا؛ فإني أفتدي منه بمالي وولدي،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r4.claim: His wealth and what he gained refers to his child, and could not benefit him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r4.anchor: ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب } يعني: ولده.

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r1.claim: Ma aghna is either a rhetorical negative question or a direct negation, explaining his ruin: nothing in his wealth saved him or brought good.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r1.anchor: {مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ} bu مَا istifhâm-ı inkârî veya doğrudan doğru nâfiyedir

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r2.claim: Ma kasab can be a relative noun or verbal noun, and may likewise be read as a rhetorical question or negation.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r2.anchor: ve kazandığı, yahut kazancı: meksûbâtı veya kesbi bu مَا, mevsul veya masdariyyedir

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r3.claim: One possible rendering asks what his wealth and earnings gained him: neither rescued him from disaster nor earned him any good.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r3.anchor: “Ne fâide verdi ona malı? Ve ne kazandı? Onu felâketten kurtaracak

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r4.claim: The reading that neither his property nor his earnings helped him better explains the ruin of both hands.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r4.anchor: lâkin “malı da fâide vermedi ona, kesbi de” mânasına olmak, iki elin hüsrânını

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r5.claim: Wealth and earnings may mean capital and its profit, inherited property and self-earned income, or all old and new possessions and gains.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r5.anchor: Malı sermayesi, kesbi de sermayesinden kazandığı kâr, hâsılât ve vâridat

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r6.claim: More broadly, kasb includes every benefit or effort counted to his account, including children, social standing, customary good works, and his plots against the Prophet.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r6.anchor: evlâdı, mevki‘-i ictimâ‘îsi, itikadınca kendine, kavmine, âdetine iyilik nâmına yaptığı işleri

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r7.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets ma kasab as Abu Lahab’s children.

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r8.claim: A reported anecdote says Abu Lahab called his children an evil acquisition after one pushed him while he tried to stop their fight.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r8.anchor: çıkarınız yanımdan bu kesb-i habîsi” demişti

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r9.claim: A Prophetic hadith says a man’s purest food comes from his own earnings and that his child is part of his earnings.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r9.anchor: her adamın yiyeceğinin en temizi kesbindendir, evlâdı da kesbindendir” diye vârid olmuştur

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r10.speaker: Dahhâk
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak reads kasb as Abu Lahab’s evil deed: plotting hostility against the Messenger.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r10.anchor: Dahhâk’ten: “Mâkesebi amel-i habîsi, yani Resûlullah’a adâvette keydidir” diye

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r11.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r11.claim: Qatada reads kasb as deeds he mistakenly thought good, like the deeds made scattered dust in Furqan 25:23.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r11.anchor: Katâde’den de “mâkesebi, bir iyilik yapıyorum zannıyla yaptığı ameldir

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r12.claim: A report says Abu Lahab claimed he could ransom himself from his nephew’s message with his wealth and children.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r12.anchor: rivayet olunmuştur ki “eğer kardeşimin oğlunun söylediği hak ise ben ondan malımı

ELMALILI:111:2-5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r13.claim: These interpretations do not conflict or restrict the meaning: kasb embraces all of them, and neither wealth nor any acquisition saved him.
ELMALILI:111:2-5/r13.anchor: Fakat bu mânaların birisi diğerine münâfî değildir, maksad tahsis değil, misâl demektir

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.claim: The opening prediction was fulfilled: because Abu Lahab did not believe in God’s oneness, he could not benefit from the Prophet’s intercession; status and wealth did not rescue him.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.anchor: Tâ risâletin bidâyetinde haber verilmiş olan bu hakikat böylece tahakkuk etmiş

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.claim: He did not repent of saying “tabban lak”; he died in ruin, and the author seeks refuge from an evil ending.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.anchor: ona تـَبًّا لَك dediğine tevbe de nasib olmayıp böyle tebâb olmuş gitmiştir

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.claim: After contrasting the good and ruined endings, the text points to monotheism and sincerity, then refuge in God, as the path to a good end.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.anchor: Şimdi biri, tesbih ve hamd ve istiğfar ile Allah’a giden, biri de hüsran

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.claim: The conclusion prepares for Ikhlas by saying that knowing God through pure monotheism and seeking His protection is the remedy for ruin.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.anchor: Allah târif edilerek tevhid ve ihlâs ile O’na ilticâ emrolunacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.claim: In year two of the Hijra Abu Lahab contracted smallpox and could not attend Badr, but sent a replacement and financially supported the polytheists; he reportedly died of grief seven days after their defeat.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.anchor: çiçek hastalığına yakalandığı için müslümanlara karşı Bedir Savaşı’na katılamamış, fakat yerine adam göndermiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r10.claim: Exegetes say what Abu Lahab earned means his children, wealth, status, and reputation; none could save him from a bad worldly end.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r10.anchor: Ebû Leheb’in kazandığı bildirilen şeyden maksadın onun çocukları, malı, mevki ve itibarı olduğunu söylemişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r11.claim: Shawkani also gives the verse as a question: what benefit did his wealth bring him, and what did he earn?
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r11.anchor: Malı ona ne fayda sağladı, o ne kazandı

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The verse joins early Meccan warnings that earthly wealth is useless in the afterlife, especially 69:28, 92:11, and 104:1–3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Auf die Nutzlosigkeit irdischen Reichtums im Jenseits insistieren frühmekkanisch

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r2.claim: The critique also belongs to broader Qur’anic criticism of possessions and a biblical topos, echoed in Psalm 39, 1 Timothy 6, and Luke 18/Mark 10.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Die letztendliche Nutzlosigkeit irdischer Reichtümer ist bereits ein biblischer Topos

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r3.claim: The particle mā can be read either as a question, asking what wealth helped him, or as a negation, saying it helped him nothing.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r3.anchor: kann mā hier sowohl als Fragepronomen („Was hat ihm sein Besitz geholfen?“) wie auch als Verneinungspartikel („Sein Besitz hat ihm nichts geholfen“) aufgefasst werden

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Bergsträßer
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r4.claim: Bergsträßer favors the negative reading because the numerous parallel formulations make negation more likely here too.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r4.anchor: mit Bergsträßer davon auszugehen, dass „die große Anzahl der Parallelen 〈…〉 auch hier die Negation als wahrscheinlicher erscheinen“

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Paret
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r5.claim: Paret takes the perfect as resultative, giving the statement a present reference; the author follows this reading.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Mit Paret ist das Perfekt wohl resultativ zu verstehen und hat somit einen Gegenwartsbezug

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r6.claim: The similar afterlife statement at 92:11 uses an imperfect instead of a perfect without an evident difference in meaning.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r6.anchor: statt des Perfekts das Imperfekt enthält, ohne dass ein offenkundiger Bedeutungsunterschied spürbar wäre

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r7.claim: It is prima facie possible to treat mā kasab as synonymous with māluhū, meaning what Abū Lahab acquired, as 7:48 uses gathering in a similar context.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Es wäre prima facie auch möglich, māluhū und mā kasab synonym aufzufassen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r8.claim: The literal acquisition reading conflicts with the Qur’an’s dominant figurative use of kasaba as committing deeds, already attested in pre-Islamic poetry.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Doch würde eine solche Lesart der sonst im Koran dominierenden übertragenen Bedeutung von kasaba „begehen“ zuwiderlaufen, die auch schon in der vorkoranischen Dichtung belegt ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r9.speaker: Rubin
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r9.claim: Rubin identifies Abū Lahab’s deeds with his service to al-ʿUzzā and his protection of Muhammad, which he later renounced.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r9.anchor: Rubin geht noch einen Schritt weiter und will die mit mā kasab, „was er begangen hat“, intendierten Handlungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r10.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r10.claim: The author warns against over-specifying the phrase through anecdotes rooted in early Islamic reception, as with interpretations of 93:3, 93:6–8, and 108:3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:2:anmerkung/r10.anchor: besteht hier aber die Gefahr einer letztlich in der anekdotischen Tendenz der frühislamischen Koranrezeption wurzelnden übertriebenen Konkretisierung koranischer Aussagen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops from a curse against an enemy called ‘Father of Flame’; all verses except verse 5 refer back to him pronominally.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.anchor: Der Text entwickelt sich aus der einleitenden Verwünschung eines als „Vater der Flammen“ bezeichneten Gegners heraus

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r2.claim: The first, still unspecified threat says the accursed man’s accumulated wealth is useless; verse 3 clarifies the afterlife setting.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r2.anchor: An den Eröffnungsvers schließt sich ein erstes, unbestimmtes Drohwort (V. 2) an

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r3.claim: The sura joins early Meccan prophetic criticism of wealth, a topos also important in the Hebrew Bible.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r3.anchor: Die Sure greift damit wie auch andere frühmekkanische Texte den Topos prophetischer Besitzkritik auf

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r7.claim: The author rejects Rubin’s cult reading: the sura never accuses them of idolatry, verse 2 instead ties wrongdoing to wealth, and pagan ritual condemnation is not prominent in other early Meccan texts.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r7.anchor: Allerdings wird der Vorwurf des Götzendienstes von der Sure selbst gar nicht erhoben

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r2.claim: The warning about wealth's false promise of immortality portrays Abū Lahab and his associates, who learned that wealth cannot protect them from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r2.anchor: He who amassed wealth and counted it over

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r3.speaker: Some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r3.claim: Some interpreters take what Abū Lahab earned to mean his sons; Islahi accepts that they ultimately failed to help him but calls this reading far-fetched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r3.anchor: Some think that they refer to his sons.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r4.speaker: Some others
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r4.claim: Other interpreters take the phrase to mean his illicit earnings; Islahi rejects this as linguistically unsuitable and redundant with the preceding clause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r4.anchor: Some others regard them to refer to his illegal earnings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r5.claim: The phrase instead refers to deeds he considered virtuous, but his evil disposition and polytheism deprived them of value before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r5.anchor: his subscription to polytheism they have no value.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p512/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p512/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p512/r1.claim: As treasurer of the Baytullāh, Abū Lahab performed welfare works for poor people and pilgrims as pretense to cover his misdeeds; these works had no divine value.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p512/r1.anchor: Such works have no value before the Almighty.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says what Abū Lahab earned refers to his children.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة عن ابن عباس قال وما كسب قال هم الولد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.claim: Following the prior sura's mass conversion, this one describes Abu Lahab as a loser who stayed outside the faith embraced by Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها دخول الناس في دين الله تعالى، أتبع بذكر من لم يدخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r6.claim: The apparent ma is negative: neither inherited wealth nor personal earnings, livestock, offspring, or trade profits could benefit Abu Lahab.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في ما أغنى عنه ماله نفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r7.claim: Another parse makes ma an interrogative in the accusative, asking what his wealth could avail.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما استفهاما في موضع نصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r8.claim: Ma in wa-ma kasab is apparently relative but may be a verbal noun; if the first ma is interrogative, the second may be as well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في قوله: وما كسب موصولة، وأجيز أن تكون مصدرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says what Abu Lahab gained was his child, with a report that a man's child is his earning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: وما كسب ولده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r10.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the gain as Abu Lahab's evil work against the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r10.anchor: وعن الضحاك: وما كسب هو عمله الخبيث في عداوة الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r11.claim: Qatada says it refers to the deeds Abu Lahab thought would benefit him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r11.anchor: وعن قتادة: وعمله الذي ظن أنه منه على شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r6.speaker: أبو لهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r6.claim: A report says Abu Lahab offered to ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew's message proved true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r6.anchor: وروي عنه أنه كان يقول: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r7.speaker: عبد الله وأبو حيوة وابن مقسم وعباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r7.claim: Reported readings include wa-ma iktasaba with an added t, passive sayuṣalla, and diminutive or hamzated forms for wife; another reading gives hammālata with tanwin and a preposition before al-haṭab.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p567/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: وما اكتسب بتاء الافتعال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r1.claim: The first “mā” is usually negative: his wealth did not protect him when ruin arrived; it may instead be interrogative, asking what his wealth accomplished.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r1.anchor: أى لم يغنى عنه ماله حين حل به التباب على أن ما نافية ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r2.claim: “What he earned” may be a relative phrase or a verbal noun meaning his earning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r2.anchor: كسبه على أن ما موصولة وجوز أن تكون مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says that if the first “mā” is interrogative, the second may also ask what he earned, implying that he earned nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان اذا كان ما الاولى استفهامية فيجوز أن تكون هذه كذلك أى وأى شىء كسب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r4.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r4.claim: Issam al-Din offers a negative reading: his wealth did not avert harm, and what he earned brought no benefit; the author objects to making wealth the subject of “earned.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r4.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن تكون نافية والمعنى ما أغنى عنه ماله مضرة وما كسب منفعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r5.claim: Al-Bahr prefers the relative reading, with an omitted object pronoun: what he gained in profits, benefits, status, and followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r5.anchor: واستظهر فى البحر موصوليتها فالعائد محذوف أى والذى كسبه به من الارباح والنتائج والمنافع والوجاهة والاتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak explains what Abu Lahab earned as his evil plotting against the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r6.anchor: أو ماله والذى كسبه من عمله الخبيث الذى هو كيده فى عداوة النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما قال الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r7.claim: Qatada interprets it as deeds he thought valuable but which became worthless, linking the expression to the Quranic image of deeds turned to scattered dust.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r7.anchor: أو من عمله الذى يظن أنه منه على شىء كقوله تعالى وقدمنا إلى ماعملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا كما قال قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say “what he earned” means his children.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومجاهد ماكسب من الولد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r9.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r9.claim: Abu Dawud transmits Aisha’s report that a man’s best food is from his own earnings and his child is part of his earnings.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r9.anchor: أخرج أبو داود عن عائشة مرفوعا أن أطيب مايأكل الرجل من كسبه وان ولده من كسبه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r10.claim: Abu Lahab reportedly boasted that he would ransom himself with wealth and children if Muhammad’s claim were true; he had three sons, two of whom accepted Islam at the conquest and were blessed by the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r10.anchor: وروى أنه كان كان يقول ان كان مايقول ابن أخى حقا فانا أفتدى منه نفسى بمالى وولدى وكان له ثلاثة أبناء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r11.claim: His son Utaybah did not convert, divorced Umm Kulthum under his father’s threat, then insulted the Prophet and divorced her himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r11.anchor: قال أبو لهب لهما رأسى ورأسكما حرام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r12.claim: Utaybah announced disbelief in the star and in the one who drew near, spat toward the Prophet without hitting him, and was cursed by the Prophet after threatening him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r12.anchor: فقال يامحمد انى كافر بالنجم اذا هوى وبالذى دنا فتدلى ثم تفل تجاه رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r13.claim: The Prophet prayed that a beast of prey attack Utaybah; on the journey to Syria a lion singled him out and killed him despite the group’s precautions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r13.anchor: فقال صلى تعالى عليه وسلم اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r14.speaker: حسان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r14.claim: The report’s account of the lion killing Utaybah is followed by a verse attributed to Hassan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262/r14.anchor: وفى ذلك يقول حسان من يرجع العام إلى أهله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r1.claim: Abu Lahab died of al-ʿadasa seven nights after Badr; his family feared contagion, left him three days until he stank, then arranged his burial.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r1.anchor: وهلك أبو لهب نفسه بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر لسبع ليال فاجتنبه أهله مخافة العدوى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r2.claim: Burial accounts differ: some say hired porters placed him in a dug grave, others that they leaned him against a wall and buried him under stones from a distance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r2.anchor: فلما خافوا العار استأجروا بعض السودان فاحتملوه ودفنوه وفى رواية حفروا له حفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r3.claim: The author says events unfolded as the Quran had foretold; Abd Allah’s reading has the intensive form “wa-mā iktasaba.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p262#2/r3.anchor: فكان الامر كما أخبر به القرآن وقرأ عبد الله وماأكتسب بناء الافتعال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that when the Prophet invited his relatives to God, Abū Lahab said he would ransom himself, wealth, and children if his nephew were right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: لما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرباءه إلى الله عز وجل قال أبو لهب: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r2.claim: His wealth could not protect him from God's punishment; he had accumulated property and owned herds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r2.anchor: أي: ما يدفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال، وكان صاحب مواش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r3.claim: The phrase mā aghnā is explained either as what does not benefit him or as the question, What use is his wealth?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r3.anchor: أي ما يغني، وقيل: أي شيء يغني عنه ماله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r4.claim: Mā kasaba can mean his children, since a person's child is part of his earnings, as stated in a Prophetic report.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r4.anchor: {وما كسب} قيل: يعني ولده، لأن ولد الإنسان من كسبه كما جاء في الحديث:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's report says the best thing a person eats is from his earnings, and his child is among what he earns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p582#2/r5.anchor: "أطيب ما يأكل أحدكم من كسبه، وإن ولده من كسبه"

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r1.claim: Ma aghna negates that his wealth helped when destruction arrived, or is a rhetorical question denying that it helped.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r1.anchor: نفي لإغناء المال عنه حين نزل به التباب أو استفهام إنكار له

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r2.claim: What he acquired may be profits, status and followers gained through wealth, what he thought his deeds would earn him, or his son Utbah, who a lion attacked on the road to Syria.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r2.anchor: من النتائج والأرباح والوجاهة والإتباع، أو عمله الذي ظن أنه ينفعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r3.claim: Abu Lahab died from smallpox a few days after Badr; his body was left until it decomposed and enslaved Black men were hired to bury it, fulfilling the unseen report.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:2-4/r3.anchor: ومات أبو لهب بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر بأيام معدودة، وترك ثلاثا حتى أنتن ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.claim: The Prophet hoped that the reader of Tabbat would not be gathered with Abu Lahab in one abode.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة تبت رجوت أن لا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب في دار واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r2.claim: Aghna means to suffice, benefit, or avert harm; the verse asks rhetorically what Abu Lahab's wealth and acquired advantages did for him, since worldly circumstances cannot save.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r2.anchor: ما أغنى } أي أجزى وناب وسد { عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r3.claim: Kasab is broader than money and includes status and useful gains produced by one's effort; none helps unless God commands it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r3.anchor: وكان المال قد تكسب منافع هي أعظم منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r4.claim: Abu Lahab used his influence and clan to oppose and discredit Muhammad in public, although he had once called him the truthful and trustworthy one.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r4.anchor: مع أنه كان قبل ذلك يناديه بالصادق الأمين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r5.claim: After Abu Lahab's son Utbah harmed Muhammad, the Prophet prayed for a beast to attack him; Abu Lahab tried to protect him on a Syrian journey, but a lion found and killed him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p570/r5.anchor: حتى قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم سلط عيله كلبا من كلابك )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r1.claim: Abu Rafi, a servant of al-Abbas, reports that while the secretly Muslim household heard Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith describe white angels on piebald horses at Badr, Abu Rafi identified them and Abu Lahab struck him; Umm al-Fadl wounded Abu Lahab with a tent pole.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r1.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r2.claim: Abu Lahab died six or seven nights later of al-adasa, a usually fatal pustule resembling plague; Arabs feared it and left his corpse unburied until it stank, then buried it from a distance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r2.anchor: فوالله ما عاش إلا سبع ليال أو ستا حتى رماه الله بالعدسة فقتله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r3.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r3.claim: Al-Qazzaz defines adasa as a pustule and says the verb عدس الرجل means that a man contracted it, paralleling طعن for being struck by plague.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r3.anchor: قال القزاز : كانت تعدي في الجاهلية قلما يسلم منها أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p571/r4.claim: The disgraceful death and burial show that nothing Abu Lahab believed could save him, an early fulfillment of the verses' prediction.

DURR-FULL:v8p666/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha applies the idea that a son is a man’s earnings to this verse, taking what Abū Lahab earned to mean his children.
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه وان ابنه من كسبه

DURR-FULL:v8p666/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r3.speaker: عطاء، مجاهد، عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports the interpretation that Abū Lahab’s wealth and earnings include his offspring; Mujāhid and ʿĀʾisha share it.
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r3.anchor: عن عطاء قال: كان يقال: ما أإنى عنه ماله وما كسب وولده كسبه

DURR-FULL:v8p666/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r4.claim: Ruqayya, the Prophet’s daughter, was married to ʿUtba son of Abū Lahab; after the surah descended, the Prophet requested a divorce, and she later married ʿUthmān.
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كانت رقيه بنت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند عتبة بن أبي لهب

DURR-FULL:v8p666/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r5.claim: Abū Lahab forced his sons ʿUtayba and ʿUtba to divorce the Prophet’s daughters; their mother Hind urged divorce because the daughters had converted.
DURR-FULL:v8p666/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال: تزوج أم كلثوم بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عتيبة بن أبي لهب

TAB:111:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:111:2/r1.claim: The verse asks what his wealth did for him or how it could repel God's displeasure from him.
TAB:111:2/r1.anchor: أيّ شيء أغنى عنه ماله ،   ودفع من سخط الله عليه

TAB:111:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:2/r2.speaker: author
TAB:111:2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains what Abū Lahab earned as his children.

TAB:111:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:111:2/r3.claim: Abū al-Ṭufayl recounts that Ibn ʿAbbās, though blind, tried to stop Abū Lahab’s sons fighting over a house; after one pushed him onto a bed, he angrily called them an evil earning.
TAB:111:2/r3.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل ،   قال :  جاء بنو أبي لهب إلى ابن عباس ،   فقاموا يختصمون في البيت

TAB:111:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:111:2/r4.claim: A report says Ibn ʿAbbās saw Abū Lahab’s sons fighting, separated them, and said they were among what their father had earned.
TAB:111:2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   أنه رأى يوما ولد أبي لهب يقتتلون ،   فجعل يحجز بينهم ويقول :  هؤلاء مما كسب

TAB:111:2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:111:2/r5.claim: Mujāhid interprets what Abū Lahab earned as his children, who are his earnings.
TAB:111:2/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ،   عن مجاهد ،   في قول الله :  {  وَما كَسَبَ } قال :  ولده هم من كسبه

DAMGHANI:v1p403/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r9.claim: Mujāhid explains mā kasaba as a child or offspring.
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r9.anchor: الكسب الولد قوله تعالى في سورة المسد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p103/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p103/r1.claim: He objects to the prior point as difficult to reconcile with God describing the person as having wealth and offspring, citing the verse about his wealth and earnings.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p103/r1.anchor: ولست أدري كيف هذا لأن الله عز وجل وصفه بالمال والولد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p200/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p200/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p200/r1.claim: The exegetes take “what he earned” to mean his child, treating offspring as a person's earnings.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p200/r1.anchor: وقال المفسرون في قوله تعالى: تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب

IBNHISHAM:v1p354/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p354/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p354/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh mocked and opposed the Prophet while his uncle and clan protected him; the passage about Abu Lahab and his wife was revealed because Umm Jamil carried thorns and scattered them on his path.
IBNHISHAM:v1p354/r1.anchor: وإنما سماها الله تعالى حمالة الحطب، لأنها كانت- فيما بلغني- تحمل الشوك فتطرحه على طريق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r1.claim: The apparent ma is a negation: his inherited wealth did not benefit him.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في { ما أغنى عنه ماله } نفي ،   أي لم يغن عنه ماله الموروث عن آبائه

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r2.claim: On the apparent reading, what he earned may mean what he acquired himself, his livestock and its offspring or benefits, or profits from his trade capital.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r2.anchor: وما كسب هو بنفسه أو ماشيته

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r3.claim: Alternatively, ma is an interrogative object asking rhetorically what his money could avail him, or where its supposed enrichment is.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r3.anchor: أي : أي شيء يغني عنه ماله على وجه التقرير والإنكار

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r4.claim: The apparent ma in wa-mā kasaba is a relative pronoun, though it may also be a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في قوله : { وما كسب } موصولة ،   وأجيز أن تكون مصدرية

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r5.claim: If the first ma is interrogative, the second can also ask what he earned—implying that he earned nothing.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r5.anchor: أي : وأي شيء كسب ؟ أي لم يكسب شيئاً

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says what he earned means his child.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : { وما كسب } ولده

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r7.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r7.claim: A hadith supports the child interpretation with the saying that a man’s child is part of his earnings.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : « ولد الرجل من كسبه »

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says what he earned was his wicked work in hostility toward the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r8.anchor: وعن الضحاك : { وما كسب } هو عمله الخبيث في عداوة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r9.claim: Qatāda says it is the deed he thought would amount to something for him.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r9.anchor: وعن قتادة : وعمله الذي ظن أنه منه على شيء

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r10.claim: Qatāda also reports Abū Lahab’s boast that, if his nephew spoke truly, he would ransom himself with his wealth and children.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r10.anchor: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقاً ،   فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r11.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r11.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads wa-mā iktasaba with the iftiʿāl tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:111:2/r11.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : وما اكتسب بتاء الافتعال

ALUSI:111:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r1.claim: The negation means Abū Lahab's wealth did not help him when destruction overtook him.
ALUSI:111:2/r1.anchor: أي لم يغن عنه ماله حين حل به التباب على أن ما نافية

ALUSI:111:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r2.claim: The first mā may instead be interrogative, parsed as an accusative direct object (‘what did it avail?’) or cognate object (‘to what extent did it avail?’).
ALUSI:111:2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية في محل نصب بما بعدها على أنها مفعول به أو مفعول مطلق

ALUSI:111:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r3.claim: Mā kasaba may be a relative pronoun, ‘what he acquired,’ or a verbal noun, ‘his earning.’
ALUSI:111:2/r3.anchor: أي والذي كسبه على أن ما موصولة وجوز أن تكون مصدرية أي وكسبه

ALUSI:111:2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:111:2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that if the first mā is interrogative, the second can be interrogative too: ‘what did he earn?’—meaning he earned nothing.
ALUSI:111:2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إذا كان ما الأولى استفهامية فيجوز أن تكون هذه كذلك أي وأي شيء كسب أي لم يكسب شيئا

ALUSI:111:2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r5.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:111:2/r5.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn allows a negative reading: his wealth did not keep harm away, and what he earned brought no benefit.
ALUSI:111:2/r5.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن تكون نافية والمعنى ما أعبد عنه ماله مضرة وما كسب منفعة

ALUSI:111:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds ʿIṣām al-Dīn's apparent parsing strange because it makes the wealth the subject of kasaba.
ALUSI:111:2/r6.anchor: وظاهره أنه جعل فاعل كسب ضمير المال وهو كما ترى

ALUSI:111:2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:111:2/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr prefers mā as a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent: what he earned through wealth, including profits, benefits, status, and followers.
ALUSI:111:2/r7.anchor: واستظهر في البحر موصوليتها فالعائد محذوف أي ولذي كسبه به من الأرباح والنتائج والمنافع والوجاهة والاتباع

ALUSI:111:2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r8.claim: Other explanations take the phrase as his wealth inherited from his father plus what he earned himself, or his wealth plus the fruits of his own work.
