ALUSI:111:2/r8.anchor: أو ما أغنى عنه ماله الموروث من أبيه والذي كسبه بنفسه أو ماله والذي كسبه من عمله الخبيث

ALUSI:111:2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI:111:2/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies what Abū Lahab earned with his wicked plotting against the Prophet.
ALUSI:111:2/r9.anchor: من عمله الخبيث الذي هو كيده في عداوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما قال الضحاك

ALUSI:111:2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:111:2/r10.claim: Qatāda identifies it as deeds he thought amounted to something, which God makes like scattered dust, as in 25:23.
ALUSI:111:2/r10.anchor: ما علموا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا } [ الفرقان : 23 ] كما قال قتادة

ALUSI:111:2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI:111:2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid interpret what he earned as his children.
ALUSI:111:2/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومجاهد ما كسب من الولد

ALUSI:111:2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r12.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI:111:2/r12.claim: Abū Dāwūd transmits from ʿĀʾisha, as a Prophetic report, that a man's best food is from his earnings and his child is part of his earnings; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:111:2/r12.anchor: أخرج أبو داود عن عائشة مرفوعا أن أطيب ما يأكل الرجل من كسبه وأن ولده من كسبه

ALUSI:111:2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r13.claim: Abū Lahab reportedly said that if his nephew were right, he would ransom himself from the consequences with his wealth and children.
ALUSI:111:2/r13.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فإنا أفتدى منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

ALUSI:111:2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r14.claim: Abū Lahab had three sons: ʿUtba and Muʿattib accepted Islam at the conquest, pleasing the Prophet, who prayed for them; they attended Ḥunayn and al-Ṭāʾif, while ʿUtayba did not convert.
ALUSI:111:2/r14.anchor: وكان له ثلاثة أبناء عتبة ومعتب وقد أسلما يوم الفتح وسر النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام بإسلامهما ودعا لهما

ALUSI:111:2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r15.speaker: صاحب كتاب الألباء
ALUSI:111:2/r15.claim: The author of Kitāb al-Albāʾ's verses praise ʿUtba and Muʿattib for becoming Muslim and warn against insulting a Muslim man.
ALUSI:111:2/r15.anchor: وفي ذلك يقول صاحب كتاب الالباء . كرهت عتيبة إذ أجرما *** وأحببت عتبة إذ أسلما

ALUSI:111:2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r16.claim: ʿUtayba was married to the Prophet's daughter Umm Kulthūm, and his brother ʿUtba to Ruqayya; after the sūra, Abū Lahab forced both sons to divorce them.
ALUSI:111:2/r16.anchor: وكانت أم كلثوم بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند عتيبة ورقية أختها عند أخيه عتبة فلما نزلت السورة

ALUSI:111:2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r17.claim: Before traveling to Syria, ʿUtayba vowed to insult Muhammad, rejected the Star and the one who drew near, spat toward the Prophet without hitting him, and divorced Umm Kulthūm.
ALUSI:111:2/r17.anchor: فقال لآتين محمدا عليه الصلاة والسلام وأوذينه فأتاه فقال يا محمد إني كافر بالنجم إذا هوى وبالذي دنا فتدلى

ALUSI:111:2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r18.claim: The Prophet prayed that a dog from among God's dogs would attack ʿUtayba; Abū Ṭālib, present, questioned why he had made that prayer.
ALUSI:111:2/r18.anchor: فأغضبه عليه الصلاة والسلام بما قال وفعل فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك وكان أبو طالب حاضرا

ALUSI:111:2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r19.claim: A monk warned the travelers that the Syrian stopping place was full of predators; Abū Lahab arranged the camels around his son for protection, but a lion found and killed ʿUtayba.
ALUSI:111:2/r19.anchor: فنزلوا منزلا فأشرف عليهم راهب من دير وقال لهم إن هذه أرض مسبعة فقال أبو لهب أغيثوني يا معشر قريش في هذه الليلة

ALUSI:111:2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r20.speaker: حسان
ALUSI:111:2/r20.claim: Ḥassān's couplet says that whoever returns to his family that year cannot be someone eaten by a lion, marking ʿUtayba's death.
ALUSI:111:2/r20.anchor: وفي ذلك يقول حسان : من يرجع العام إلى أهله *** فما أكيل السبع بالراجع

ALUSI:111:2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r21.claim: Abū Lahab died of ʿadsa seven nights after Badr; fearing contagion like plague, his family avoided him for three days until he decomposed, then buried him through hired carriers.
ALUSI:111:2/r21.anchor: وهلك أبو لهب نفسه بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر لسبع ليال فاجتنبه أهله مخافة العدوى وكانت قريش تتقيها كالطاعون

ALUSI:111:2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r22.claim: Alternative burial reports say his family either pushed him into a dug pit with a stick and covered him with stones, or propped him against a wall and threw stones until he was hidden.
ALUSI:111:2/r22.anchor: وفي رواية حفروا له حفرة ودفعوه بعود حتى وقع فيها فقذفوه بالحجارة حتى واروه وفي أخرى أنهم لم يحفروا له

ALUSI:111:2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:111:2/r23.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that events unfolded as the Qurʾān had foretold.
ALUSI:111:2/r23.anchor: فكان الأمر كما أخبر به القرآن

ALUSI:111:2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:111:2/r24.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI:111:2/r24.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads وما اكتسب, using the iftiʿāl form.
ALUSI:111:2/r24.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وما اكتسب بناء الافتعال

BAGHAWI:111:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI:111:2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that after the Messenger summoned his close relatives to God, Abū Lahab said he would ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew’s claim were true; the verse was then revealed.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : لما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرباءه إلى الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI:111:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:111:2/r2.claim: Baghawī glosses the clause as asking what benefit Abū Lahab's wealth could bring him.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r2.anchor: { ما أغنى عنه ماله } أي ما يغني

BAGHAWI:111:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:111:2/r3.claim: An alternative gloss asks what thing his wealth could avail him.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r3.anchor: وقيل : أي شيء يغني عنه ماله

BAGHAWI:111:2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:111:2/r4.claim: The wealth Abū Lahab gathered could not ward off God's punishment from him.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r4.anchor: أي : ما يدفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال

BAGHAWI:111:2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:111:2/r5.claim: An alternative gloss takes what Abū Lahab earned to mean his child, since a person's child is considered part of his earnings, as the hadith indicates.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r5.anchor: قيل : يعني ولده ؛ لأن ولد الإنسان من كسبه ، كما جاء في الحديث

BAGHAWI:111:2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:111:2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:111:2/r6.claim: The author cites an unattributed hadith saying that the best food a person eats comes from his earnings and that his child is from his earnings.
BAGHAWI:111:2/r6.anchor: أطيب ما يأكل أحدكم من كسبه ، وإن ولده من كسبه

BAYDAWI:111:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r1.claim: The clause either denies that his wealth benefited him when destruction came, or rhetorically asks in denial whether it benefited him.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r1.anchor: نفي لإغناء المال عنه حين نزل به التباب ، أو استفهام إنكار له

BAYDAWI:111:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r2.claim: On the interrogative reading, mā is in the accusative position.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r2.anchor: أو استفهام إنكار له ، ومحلها النصب

BAYDAWI:111:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r3.claim: Mā kasab may mean his earnings or acquisitions through wealth, such as offspring, profits, prestige, and followers.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r3.anchor: وكسبه أو مكسوبه بماله من النتائج والأرباح والوجاهة والاتباع

BAYDAWI:111:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r4.claim: It may instead mean deeds he thought would benefit him.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r4.anchor: أو عمله الذي ظن أنه ينفعه

BAYDAWI:111:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r5.claim: Another identification is his son ʿUtba, whom a lion mauled on the road to Syria.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r5.anchor: أو ولده عتبة وقد افترسه أسد في طريق الشام

BAYDAWI:111:2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r6.claim: Abu Lahab died of al-ʿadasa a few days after Badr, was left three days until decomposed, and was finally buried by hired Sudanese; the account treats this as fulfilled prediction.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r6.anchor: مات أبو لهب بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر بأيام معدودة ، وترك ثلاثا حتى أنتن ، ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

BAYDAWI:111:2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:111:2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:111:2/r7.claim: Bayḍāwī calls the passage a report of the unseen whose fulfillment matched what happened.
BAYDAWI:111:2/r7.anchor: فهو إخبار عن الغيب طابقه وقوعه

BIQAI:111:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r1.claim: After the emphatic announcement of ruin, the verse answers disbelievers who presumed wealth, children, and strength could secure them, declaring worldly circumstances useless.
BIQAI:111:2/r1.anchor: ولما أوقع سبحانه الإخبار بهلاكه على هذا الوجه المؤكد لما كان لصاحب القصة وغيره من الكفار من التكذيب بلسان حاله وقاله لما له من المال والولد

BIQAI:111:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r2.claim: The construction may be read as an informative statement or as a rebuking rhetorical question.

BIQAI:111:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r3.claim: Aghnā means to suffice, benefit, or meet a need; ‘against him’ means against Abū Lahab, the wretched outcast banished from mercy and punished.
BIQAI:111:2/r3.anchor: أي أجزى وناب وسد { عنه } أي عن أبي لهب الشقي الطريد المبعود عن الرحمة

BIQAI:111:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r4.claim: His abundant wealth was the kind people customarily expect to save them from destruction, yet it did not.
BIQAI:111:2/r4.anchor: { ماله } أي الكثير الذي جرت العادة بأنه ينجي من الهلاك

BIQAI:111:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r5.claim: What one earns is broader than money: property can produce greater benefits such as status, and a person may prosper through achievements gained by effort without wealth.
BIQAI:111:2/r5.anchor: ولما كان الكسب أعم من المال ، وكان المال قد يكسب منافع هي أعظم منه من الجاه وغيره

BIQAI:111:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r6.claim: Nothing benefits except what God commands; ‘what he earned’ includes children, companions, and clan prestige, which Abū Lahab used to harm and deny the Prophet publicly and discourage belief despite formerly calling him truthful and trustworthy.
BIQAI:111:2/r6.anchor: مبيناً أنه لا ينفع إلا ما أمر الله به

BIQAI:111:2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:111:2/r7.claim: The Prophet prayed that God set one of His dogs against ʿUtba, Abū Lahab's son, who had severely mistreated him.
BIQAI:111:2/r7.anchor: حتى قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " اللهم سلط عليه كلباً من كلابك "

BIQAI:111:2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r8.claim: Abū Lahab feared the Prophet's prayer and sent his son toward Syria with companions instructed to protect him, but a lion found and killed him despite their precautions.
BIQAI:111:2/r8.anchor: فكان أبو لهب يعرف أن هذه الدعوة لا بد أن تدركه ، فلما حان الأمر ، وكان قد آن ما أراد صاحب العز الشامخ

BIQAI:111:2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r9.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI:111:2/r9.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ recounts that at Badr Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith described the defeat and white riders on piebald horses in the sky who overwhelmed the Meccans; Rāfiʿ recognized them as angels.
BIQAI:111:2/r9.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه- وكان جالساً في حجرة في المسجد يبري نبلاً

BIQAI:111:2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r10.speaker: أبو سفيان بن الحارث
BIQAI:111:2/r10.claim: Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith told Abū Lahab that at Badr the Muslims routed them, taking prisoners as they wished, and that white riders in the sky could not be resisted.
BIQAI:111:2/r10.anchor: كان منهم ابن أخيه أبو سفيان بن الحارث فقال : هلم يا ابن أخي ، فعندك الخبر

BIQAI:111:2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r11.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI:111:2/r11.claim: Abū Lahab struck the weak Abū Rāfiʿ, knocked him down, and beat him after he called the unseen fighters angels; Umm al-Faḍl split Abū Lahab's head with a tent pole and rebuked him for attacking her servant while his master was away.
BIQAI:111:2/r11.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه- وكان جالساً في حجرة في المسجد يبري نبلاً

BIQAI:111:2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r12.speaker: أبو رافع
BIQAI:111:2/r12.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says Abū Lahab left humiliated and died six or seven nights later when God struck him with al-ʿadasa.
BIQAI:111:2/r12.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه

BIQAI:111:2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r13.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI:111:2/r13.claim: Al-Qazzāz describes al-ʿadasa as a usually fatal, plague-like pustule resembling a lentil; in pre-Islamic times it was thought contagious and few survived it.
BIQAI:111:2/r13.anchor: والعدسة بثرة تشبه العدسة تخرج في مواضع من الجسد من جنس الطاعون تقتل غالباً ، قال القزاز : كانت تعدي في الجاهلية

BIQAI:111:2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r14.claim: The disease is called ʿadasa; one says ʿadasa al-rajul or huwa maʿdūs, as one says ṭuʿina or maṭʿūn for being struck by plague.
BIQAI:111:2/r14.anchor: تقول : عدس الرجل فهو معدوس ، كما تقول : طعن فهو مطعون

BIQAI:111:2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r15.claim: Because Arabs feared al-ʿadasa, Abū Lahab's body was left unburied for three days until it stank, then hired Sudanese men buried it; another account says they pushed it into a distant pit with poles and threw stones and earth from afar.
BIQAI:111:2/r15.anchor: ولأجل تشاؤم العرب بها ترك أبو لهب من غير دفن ثلاثاً ، حتى أنتن ، ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

BIQAI:111:2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:111:2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI:111:2/r16.claim: The distant stoning of the grave became a custom, and Abū Lahab is still stoned; this was an early sign of the verses' miraculous truth, since nothing he thought would save him prevented his disgrace among Arabs.
BIQAI:111:2/r16.anchor: فكان ذلك سنة في رجمه ، فهو يرجم إلى الآن ، وذلك من أول إعجاز هذه الآيات

DURR:111:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:111:2/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR:111:2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says that “what he earned” refers to his child, noting that a man's son is part of his earning.
DURR:111:2/r1.anchor: عائشة قالت : إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه ، وإن ابنه من كسبه ، ثم قرأ { ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب } قالت : وما كسب ولده

DURR:111:2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:111:2/r2.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد وعائشة
DURR:111:2/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ transmits the gloss that “what he earned” means his child; Mujāhid and ʿĀʾisha are also named as holding this view.
DURR:111:2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء قال : كان يقال : { ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب } ، وولده كسبه ، ومجاهد وعائشة قالاه

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r1.claim: On the negative reading, none of Abu Lahab's worldly circumstances helped him once torment after death was decreed for him.

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the interrogative is rhetorical: where was the benefit of his wealth and earnings?
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون { ما } استفهاماً على وجه التقرير ، أي أين الغناء الذي لماله ولكسبه ؟

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r3.claim: “What he earned” may mean worldly property, such as real estate.
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r3.anchor: يراد به عرض الدنيا من عقار

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the wording highlights that he labored to acquire this wealth rather than receiving it freely through inheritance, a gift, or similar means.
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r4.anchor: أو ليكون الكلام دالاً على أنه أتعب فيه نفسه ، لم يجئه عفوا ، لا بميراث وهبة ونحوه

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r5.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r5.claim: Many exegetes say “what he earned” means his sons, so the verse pairs his wealth with his children.
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r5.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين : المراد ب { ما كسب } بنوه ، فكأنه قال : { ما أغنى عنه ماله } وولده

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r6.claim: The Prophet said a man's best earnings come from his own labor and that his child is among his earnings, supporting the sons interpretation.
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r6.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " خير ما كسب الرجل من عمل يده ، وإن ولد الرجل من كسبه

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r7.claim: As Abu Lahab's sons quarreled, one pushed the blind Ibn Abbas while he intervened; Ibn Abbas angrily called them “vile earnings.”
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r7.anchor: فتنازعوا وتدافعوا ، فقام ابن عباس ليحجز بينهم ، فدفعه أحدهم ، فوقع على فراشه ، وكان قد كف بصره فغضب وصاح : أخرجوا عني الكسب الخبيث

IBNATIYYA:111:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r8.speaker: الأعمش وأبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read “وما اكتسب” (“and what he acquired”).
IBNATIYYA:111:2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأبي بن كعب : «وما اكتسب »

IBNKATHIR:111:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and other authorities understand 'what he earned' to mean Abu Lahab's children.
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره : { وَمَا كَسَبَ } يعني : ولده

IBNKATHIR:111:2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r2.speaker: عائشة، مجاهد، عطاء، الحسن، ابن سيرين
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r2.claim: Aisha, Mujahid, Ata, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin are also reported to give the gloss 'his children.'
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r2.anchor: وروي عن عائشة ،   ومجاهد ،   وعطاء ،   والحسن ،   وابن سيرين ،   مثله

IBNKATHIR:111:2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that when the Messenger called his people to faith, Abu Lahab said that if his nephew were truthful, he would ransom himself from punishment on Judgment Day with his wealth and children; the verse was then revealed.
IBNKATHIR:111:2/r3.anchor: وذكر عن ابن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دعا قومه إلى الإيمان ،   قال أبو لهب : إذا كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

MAWARDI:111:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:2/r1.claim: One explanation of مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ is that his wealth did not ward anything off from him.

MAWARDI:111:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:111:2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ as meaning that his wealth did not benefit him.

MAWARDI:111:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI:111:2/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says his مال was his herds, since Abū Lahab owned grazing livestock.
MAWARDI:111:2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد أغنامه ؛ لأنه كان صاحب سائمة ،   قاله أبو العالية .

MAWARDI:111:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:2/r4.claim: Another view understands his wealth as both inherited property (talīd) and acquired property (ṭārif).
MAWARDI:111:2/r4.anchor: أنه أراد تليده وطارفه ،   والتليد : الموروث ،   والطارف : المكتسب .

MAWARDI:111:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:111:2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets what Abū Lahab earned as his wicked deeds.

MAWARDI:111:2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:111:2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets what he earned as his children.

MAWARDI:111:2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r7.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:111:2/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet says, “Your children are among your earnings,” supporting the interpretation of what he earned as offspring.
MAWARDI:111:2/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال :  "  أولادكم من كسبكم

MAWARDI:111:2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:2/r8.claim: Abū Lahab’s son ʿUtba matched his father’s hostility: after Sūrat al-Najm was revealed, he blasphemed, spat at the Prophet, and left for Syria; the Prophet prayed against him, and a lion killed him.
MAWARDI:111:2/r8.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  اللهم سلط عليه كلباً من كلابك  "  ،   فأكله الأسد

MAWARDI:111:2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:2/r9.claim: One view says his wealth and earnings could not aid him in his hostility toward the Prophet.
MAWARDI:111:2/r9.anchor: أحدهما : في عداوته النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI:111:2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:2/r10.claim: Another view says they could not save him from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
MAWARDI:111:2/r10.anchor: الثاني : في دفع النار عنه يوم القيامة .

NASAFI:111:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:2/r1.claim: The first ما is negative, saying Abu Lahab’s wealth did not avail him.

NASAFI:111:2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:2/r2.claim: Nasafi says وَمَا كَسَبَ is nominative; ما may be relative, meaning what he acquired, or a verbal noun, meaning his acquisition.
NASAFI:111:2/r2.anchor: موصولة أو مصدرية ، أي ومكسوبه أو وكسبه

NASAFI:111:2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:2/r3.claim: The wealth that failed him may be what he inherited from his father, what he earned himself, or his old and newly acquired wealth.
NASAFI:111:2/r3.anchor: أي لم ينفعه ماله الذي ورثه من أبيه ، أو الذي كسبه بنفسه ، أو ماله التالد والطارف

NASAFI:111:2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI:111:2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that what Abu Lahab acquired means his children.
NASAFI:111:2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما كسب ولده

NASAFI:111:2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:2/r5.speaker: أبو لهب
NASAFI:111:2/r5.claim: An unattributed report quotes Abu Lahab saying that if his nephew’s claim were true, he would ransom himself from it with his wealth and children.
NASAFI:111:2/r5.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقاً فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

QURTUBI:111:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:2/r1.claim: His wealth and what he acquired in status could not ward God's punishment from him.
QURTUBI:111:2/r1.anchor: أي ما دفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال ، ولا ما كسب من جاه .

QURTUBI:111:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:111:2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets what he earned as his children, since a man's child is his earning.
QURTUBI:111:2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد : من الولد ، وولد الرجل من كسبه .

QURTUBI:111:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r3.speaker: الأعمش، ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:111:2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ‘wa-ma-ktasaba’ (‘and what he acquired’), transmitting this reading from Ibn Masud.
QURTUBI:111:2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش " وما اكتسب " ورواه عن ابن مسعود .

QURTUBI:111:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r4.speaker: أبو الطفيل
QURTUBI:111:2/r4.claim: Abu al-Tufayl recounts that when Abu Lahab's sons fought before Ibn Abbas, one pushed him as he tried to separate them; Ibn Abbas angrily called them ‘evil earnings,’ meaning his children.
QURTUBI:111:2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الطفيل : جاء بنو أبي لهب يختصمون عند ابن عباس ، فاقتتلوا

QURTUBI:111:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:111:2/r5.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the best food a man eats is from his own earning, and his child is part of his earning; Abu Dawud records it.
QURTUBI:111:2/r5.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه ، وإن ولده من كسبه "

QURTUBI:111:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:111:2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Muhammad warned his clan of the Fire, Abu Lahab said he would ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew was right; this verse was then revealed.
QURTUBI:111:2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لما أنذر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشيرته بالنار ، قال أبو لهب : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

QURTUBI:111:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:2/r7.claim: The first ma may be a negation (‘his wealth did not avail him’) or an interrogative (‘what did his wealth avail him?’).
QURTUBI:111:2/r7.anchor: و " ما " في قوله : { ما أغنى } : يجوز أن تكون نفيا ، ويجوز أن تكون استفهاما

QURTUBI:111:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:2/r8.claim: The second ma may be a relative pronoun (‘what he earned’) or, with the verb, a verbal noun (‘his earning’).
QURTUBI:111:2/r8.anchor: و " ما " الثانية : يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي ، ويجوز أن تكون مع الفعل مصدرا

RAZI:111:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r1.claim: The first mā may be an interrogative of denial: what effect could Abū Lahab’s wealth and earnings have in averting punishment? Even Qarūn’s wealth and Sulaymān’s kingdom could not avert death.
RAZI:111:2/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما بمعنى الإنكار

RAZI:111:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, mā is a negation: the verse states that wealth and earnings did not benefit him.
RAZI:111:2/r2.anchor: يكون ذلك إخبارا بأن المال والكسب لا ينفع

RAZI:111:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r3.claim: The mā in “what he earned” is nominative and may be a relative pronoun (“what he earned”) or a verbal noun (“his earning”).
RAZI:111:2/r3.anchor: ما كسب ) مرفوع وما موصولة أو مصدرية

RAZI:111:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r4.claim: A report says Abū Lahab claimed he would ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew’s message were true, so this verse was revealed.
RAZI:111:2/r4.anchor: إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي

RAZI:111:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r5.claim: One explanation takes his wealth and earnings as principal capital and its profits.
RAZI:111:2/r5.anchor: لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله يعني رأس المال

RAZI:111:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r6.claim: Another takes the wealth as livestock and what he earned from their offspring and produce.
RAZI:111:2/r6.anchor: أن المال هو الماشية وما كسب من نسلها

RAZI:111:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r7.claim: A third distinguishes the wealth inherited from his father from what he acquired himself.
RAZI:111:2/r7.anchor: { ماله } الذي ورثه من أبيه والذي كسبه بنفسه

RAZI:111:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:111:2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “what he earned” means his children, citing Prophetic sayings that a man’s child is his earning and that a person and his wealth belong to his father.
RAZI:111:2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { ما كسب } ولده

RAZI:111:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r9.claim: A supporting report says Abū Lahab’s sons fought; when he intervened, one pushed him down, and he angrily called them “the foul earnings.”
RAZI:111:2/r9.anchor: وروي أن بني أبي لهب احتكموا إليه فاقتتلوا

RAZI:111:2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r10.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI:111:2/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes it to mean his wealth and evil deeds, including his plotting against the Messenger.

RAZI:111:2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r11.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:111:2/r11.claim: Qatāda says “what he earned” means deeds he thought would benefit him, like deeds rendered as scattered dust.
RAZI:111:2/r11.anchor: قال قتادة : { وما كسب } أي عمله

RAZI:111:2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:111:2/r12.claim: The past-tense “did not avail” is more emphatic than the future tense in Sūrat al-Layl, as in other Qurʾānic past-tense expressions.

RAZI:111:2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:111:2/r13.claim: Some say the wealth and earnings failed to help him in opposing the Messenger.

RAZI:111:2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:2/r14.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:111:2/r14.claim: Others say wealth and earnings failed to save him from the Fire, as the next verse states.
RAZI:111:2/r14.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل لم يغنيا عنه في دفع النار
